title: Only one Indian woman had ever been elected a Fellow of the Royal Society. In 2026, a second one joined her.

sources.text: The South First - Former WHO Chief Scientist Dr Soumya Swaminathan elected Fellow of Royal Society
GKToday - Soumya Swaminathan inducted as Fellow of the Royal Society

caption:
Only one Indian woman had ever been elected a Fellow of the Royal Society. In 2026, a second one joined her.

The former WHO Chief Scientist and physician-researcher became only the second Indian woman ever elected FRS, after vaccine scientist Gagandeep Kang in 2019.

She now chairs the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation and serves as Principal Advisor to India's National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme, building on decades of work on TB, HIV and global health policy at the WHO.

Swaminathan's induction extends a family's scientific legacy into one of science's most selective societies - proof that India's health research can set the global standard, not just follow it.
